source.title: Analysis of Convolutions, Non-linearity and Depth in Graph Neural Networks using Neural Tangent Kernel
source.authors: Mahalakshmi Sabanayagam; P. Esser; Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and experimental descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies how GCN depth and skip connections affect class information and reports trained GCN accuracy by depth on Cora. Its main analysis uses NTK class separability rather than training classification error, so it is a conceptual test of the depth and shortcut claims.
record.gate_note: The paper's cited results about initialization and other prior work are not rows. NTK kernel separability and trained Cora accuracies are reported by this study and bear on depth and shortcuts. Figure-only NTK heatmaps and plots are not converted into numerical rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes GCN representation loss through over-smoothing, using NTK class separability and semi-supervised node prediction accuracy. It does not measure depth-dependent training classification error or its prevention by identity residual shortcuts in the networks V3 names. Initialization and trainability results associated with V4 are cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors conclude that vanilla GCN kernels lose class information with depth through over-smoothing, while their input skip connections retain class information even at infinite depth under the theoretical assumptions. Row normalization better preserves community structure in the studied settings, with a core-periphery exception when no community structure exists. These conclusions concern representation and prediction; the authors acknowledge that kernel class separability does not capture every MSE or accuracy trend.
record.recipe_differences: Uses infinite-width graph NTK analysis and class separability, plus selected trained GCN accuracy experiments on Cora; the claim concerns gradient-trained large non-convex networks and training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks. The paper does not evaluate the original recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth changes class separability and reported trained Cora accuracy; convolution normalization changes class-information preservation; skip connections retain class information at greater depth. In core-periphery graphs without community structure, Ssym retains graph structure while Srow is a constant kernel.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report declining Cora node prediction accuracy with increasing vanilla GCN depth, using linear and ReLU activations and symmetric or row normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing vanilla GCN depth can reduce semi-supervised node prediction accuracy on Cora.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated population DC-SBM assumptions, vanilla GCN NTK class separability tends to zero with depth; synthetic and real-data analyses illustrate related losses of class structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated graph convolution can erase community class information from vanilla GCN neural tangent kernels.

fits_no_version.finding: Skip-PC and Skip-α retain nonzero population NTK class separability at infinite depth under the stated assumptions, with supporting finite-depth kernel illustrations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-feature skip connections can preserve community class information in deep GCN neural tangent kernels.

record.problems: The main evidence is theoretical and based on an infinite-width NTK with assumptions including population DC-SBM and, in key derivations, orthonormal features. Real-data validation is largely qualitative and presented as heatmaps; accuracy values in the depth plots are figure-only. The paper itself notes that class separability does not capture every trend in MSE and accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numerical rows were available for the figure-only accuracy plots or NTK heatmaps beyond the aggregate depth groups retained. Figures 1–24 include additional graph, convolution, feature, skip-connection and dataset conditions; detailed numerical values are not stated in the text and were not reconstructed from the figures.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and the stated recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Higher training error with depth in plain batch-normalized image convolutional networks; prevention by identity residual shortcuts; deep plain tanh initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Effects of initialization choices on training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth. Related work is discussed without an original comparison.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 verdicts should be removed. Similar depth and skip-connection trends in a different construct do not constitute support or a scope limitation for training-error degradation.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, and early stopping are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and student width relative to teacher width are not tested.

No CIFAR-10 or ImageNet training-error comparisons; the paper studies GCNs, including trained accuracy on Cora and NTK class information on Cora, Citeseer and synthetic graphs. It does not report whether plain networks stall in training classification error.
The paper does not compare initialization schemes or test initialization-matched training speed or trainable depth. A cited discussion of other initialization work is not a test.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature, sharpness and divergence are not tested.
Batch normalization is not tested or compared with Fixup; the paper's skip connections are not a normalization comparison.

rows.measure: Average difference between in-class and out-of-class blocks of the population NTK (class separability); qualitative class-information preservation in NTK plots
rows.value: Class separability converges to 0 as d → ∞ for all four vanilla convolutions; the gap decreases with depth. Figure-only NTK values for specific depths.
rows.locator: Section 5.1, Corollary 1 and discussion; Sections 5.2, 7; Appendix C.3–C.5
rows.note: NTK class information is a proxy rather than training classification error. On Cora and Citeseer, the authors describe qualitative retention patterns; most plotted values are not stated numerically. The text says Srow retains class structure better in the studied settings, with some stated exceptions for core-periphery graphs without community structure.
rows.check: NTK class separability measures representation of community labels, not training classification error or optimization failure. Its decay is an explicit result, but cannot establish V3. The row also combines theoretical, synthetic and real-data conditions.
